# Full English translation of dndsheets

## Context

The mod is currently a mix of English and Spanish across almost every layer — not just the
translation files. Three exploration passes over the repo found:

- `lang/en_us.json` (main mod) is 99.7% clean English — only 5 keys leak Spanish menu-name
  references.
- The Java source is **overwhelmingly Spanish**: 269 of 284 `.java` files contain Spanish text
  (comments and/or string literals), 6,277 accented-character occurrences total. Chat/command
  feedback built with `Component.literal("...")` (which bypasses the translation system
  entirely) is Spanish in ~30 places across ~20 files — this is what a player/DM actually sees
  mid-session and is the most likely trigger for "the mod is only partially translated."
- Command-tree argument names and one subcommand (`/dndchar mejora`) are Spanish words, visible
  in tab-completion and usage syntax.
- Two content JSON files (`feats.json`, `presets.json`) embed raw Spanish prose/names with no
  translation key at all — `presets.json` is a known hard case (see below).
- Enum `label()` methods (`MagicSchool`, `CreatureType`, `CreatureSize`, `Condition`) bake
  Spanish display text into Java, separate from the intentionally-Spanish internal storage keys.
- The user confirmed scope is **everything**, including developer-only Java comments and
  self-test assertion messages, and confirmed Spanish command literals/arguments should be
  **renamed cleanly with no backward-compat aliases**.

The one genuinely hard case is `presets.json`'s 24 class/subclass names: a project memory
(confirmed by reading `tools/content_lang_keys.py:30-36`, which deliberately excludes this file)
says the preset name is **written directly** into the sheet's free-text `characterClass` field,
and `SpellSlots.casterFor` used to be described as deducing spellcasting by substring-matching
that text. Reading the actual code shows this is **already bilingual-tolerant**
(`SpellSlots.java:52-79`, `Config.hitDieFor`, `Config.WeaponDefault.allowsClass` all match
English *and* Spanish substrings already), which substantially de-risks this phase versus a
from-scratch id-based redesign — see Phase 6.

Goal: every layer of the mod — player-facing text, command syntax, content data, enum display
labels, hardcoded registry names, Java comments, and self-test messages — ends up in English,
without breaking the existing self-test suite (`gradlew build`, 3 test suites, 60+ checks) or
silently corrupting already-saved player data (`Condition` is the one place persisted data is at
stake).

## Verification tools available (from project memory + confirmed in code)

- `gradlew build` runs all 3 self-tests without a Forge runtime; `gradlew testJsonContent` runs
  just the core one. No Gradle daemon on this machine — cold build ~25-35s. **Capture stderr**:
  `cmd /c "gradlew build 2>&1"` (PowerShell alone drops `AssertionError` output).
  Note: this repo is normally driven from PowerShell — use the `cmd /c "... 2>&1"` wrapper form
  shown above rather than bash-style redirection.
- `checkChatMessagesAreTranslatable` (`JsonContentSelfTest.java:~3483-3557`) already fails the
  build on stray prose `Component.literal(...)` outside `/command/` files, and tracks a counter
  `enComandos` of tolerated command-file literals, capped `<= 86` with a `ponytail:` comment
  saying explicitly this cap exists so the count doesn't grow, and "lowering it to 0 is the
  batch that's missing" — confirmed at `JsonContentSelfTest.java:3495-3507`. Phase 2 is that
  missing batch; **lower the cap as literals are converted, don't leave it at 86**.
  - Reading it more closely: this check does not need blanket exemption or restructuring — its
    file/dir partitioning (`/command/` vs. elsewhere) already matches this plan's phase
    boundaries. No changes to the check's *logic* are needed, only to the cap constant as Phase
    2 converts literals.
- `checkTranslationKeysExist` catches any `Component.translatable("key")` used in code without a
  matching `en_us.json` entry.
- `checkContentNamesAreTranslated` is the established pattern for content-name-as-key (used for
  spells/monsters/items/weapons); `presets.json` was deliberately excluded — Phase 6 keeps it
  excluded (see design below) rather than extending this check.
- Visible-text convention: edit `en_us.json` **and** `es_es.json` (alphabetical order), then run
  `python tools/sync_lang_variants.py` to propagate to the other 6 `es_*` variants.
  `sync_lang_variants.py:18` regex-parses a `SPANISH_VARIANTS = {...}` block out of
  `JsonContentSelfTest.java` — don't reflow that declaration across lines while editing nearby
  text (relevant to Phase 8).
- Content pack JSON (`src/main/resources/dndsheets/defaults/*.json`) is hand-formatted, ~14,000
  lines total — edit with targeted text substitution (same approach as `tools/content_lang_keys.py`),
  never a full JSON parse+dump, or unrelated lines reflow.
- No network/protocol changes are expected anywhere in this plan except possibly `Condition`
  (Phase 5) — if `checkNetworkShape`/`checkNetworkWire` fails there, it prints the new hash to
  paste into `DndsheetsMod`'s `NETWORK_SHAPE`/`ORDER`/`WIRE` constants; bump `PROTOCOL_VERSION`
  and note why above it. Phase 5's design avoids touching the wire format on purpose, so this
  should not trigger, but is called out as the one checkpoint where it plausibly could.

## Phased plan

Ordered safest/most mechanical → most invasive, with the two persisted-data risks (`Condition`,
`presets.json`) sequenced back-to-back near the end of the code-behavior phases.

### Phase 0 — Baseline
Run `cmd /c "gradlew build 2>&1"` once before touching anything, to confirm a clean starting
point. No file changes.

### Phase 1 — `lang/en_us.json` cleanup (5 leaked keys)
Fix the Spanish text leaked into `chat.dndsheets.character.setup_hint`,
`gui.dndsheets.guide.page.skills` (2 spots), `gui.dndsheets.guide.page.subclass`. Two of the five
reference the literal command `/dndchar mejora` — **defer those two specific edits to land in
the same commit as Phase 3** (command rename), so this file isn't touched twice for the same
reason. Fix the other 3 now.
**Verify:** `gradlew testJsonContent`.

### Phase 2 — Hardcoded Spanish `Component.literal(...)` in chat/command feedback (~30 calls, ~20 files)
Files: `command/CharacterCommand.java`, `CharacterOptionsCommand.java`, `EncounterCommand.java`,
`PresetCommand.java`, `MagicItemCommand.java`, `MonsterCommand.java`, `WeaponCommand.java`,
`TraitCommand.java`, `SpellCommand.java`, `SheetCommand.java`, `ContentCommands.java`,
`RollLogCommand.java`, `JournalCommand.java`, `TurnCommand.java`,
`dungeon/.../command/DungeonCommand.java`, `ChatFeedback.java`, `CharacterSetupScreen.java`,
`GuideBook.java`, `NameTagHp.java`, `network/CharacterSheetOpenMessage.java`,
`client/gui/CharacterSheetScreen.java:999`, `dungeon/.../DungeonTraceScreen.java`.

Convert each `Component.literal("...Spanish...")` to `Component.translatable(key, args...)`,
add the key to `en_us.json` **and** `es_es.json` (English text in en_us, the original Spanish
prose moved into es_es as its value), then `python tools/sync_lang_variants.py`.

**Verify:** `gradlew testJsonContent` — watch `enComandos` in
`checkChatMessagesAreTranslatable` drop as literals convert; **lower the `<= 86` cap
(`JsonContentSelfTest.java:3506`) to match the new true count** once done (ideally 0). Manual
grep for remaining `Component.literal("` with accented chars under `/command/` afterward, since
the self-test only fails on cap breach, not on nonzero count.

### Phase 3 — Command tree rename (breaking, no aliases — per user decision)
`Commands.literal("mejora")` → `"improve"` (`CharacterCommand.java`). Argument names:
`"nombre"→"name"`, `"categoria"→"category"`, `"objetivo"→"target"`, `"cantidad"→"amount"`,
`"jugador"→"player"`, `"clase"→"class"`, `"nivel"→"level"`, `"valor"→"value"`, `"tipo"→"type"`
across `CharacterCommand.java`, `CharacterOptionsCommand.java`, `DistanceCommand.java`,
`RollLogCommand.java`, `MonsterCommand.java`, `SheetCommand.java`, `WeaponCommand.java`,
`TurnCommand.java`. Every `context.getArgument("nombre", ...)` call site in the same file must
change in lockstep with its declaration — a missed one is a compile error, which is self-checking.
Do this **after** Phase 1/2 so no lang key or chat message still references the old command
name once it's gone; grep lang files and all `Component.literal`/`translatable` string
arguments for `mejora` afterward as a final check.
**Verify:** `gradlew build` (compile failure catches missed rename sites).

### Phase 4 — Species submodule hardcoded Spanish names
Files: `species/src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/species/RaceRegistry.java`,
`BackgroundRegistry.java`, `DndsheetsSpeciesMod.java`.

These are the **fallback-only picker path** (used only when the Origins addon isn't installed —
the primary Origins-driven path already has full 8-language support via
`dndsheets_species/lang/*.json`, unrelated to this fix). Direct literal swap, not a new key
system — reuse the exact English wording already present in `origin.dndsheets_species.<id>.name`
lang keys for the same ids where they exist (e.g. `"acolyte"` → `"Acolyte"`), so the two paths
stay consistent. Also translate `RaceRegistry.java`'s Spanish description string(s) directly (raw
text, same convention as `items.json`/`feats.json` descriptions — not keyed).

Also check `CharacterOptionsRegistry.java` (the core-mod equivalent fallback picker source) for
the same hardcoded-Spanish-names pattern — confirm during implementation whether it's a separate
source from `PresetRegistry`/`presets.json`, and if so apply the same swap.

**Verify:** `gradlew build`; check `species/src/test/.../SpeciesSelfTest.java` for any assertion
on exact Spanish strings and update it in the same commit if found. Manual grep for remaining
accented chars in the touched files.

### Phase 5 — Enum `label()` display text
Files: `MagicSchool.java`, `CreatureType.java`, `CreatureSize.java`, `Condition.java`.

- `MagicSchool`/`CreatureType`: change only the `label()` switch bodies to English — the
  internal Spanish `key`/English-alias arrays used for JSON parsing stay untouched (storage
  format, not display). Confirm the paint sites (`SpellRegistry.java:226`,
  `MonsterRegistry.java:348-349`) write into display-only JSON output, not something re-parsed
  expecting the Spanish form.
- `CreatureSize.label()` currently returns the Spanish `key` verbatim (no separate switch) —
  add one, after confirming its only consumer (`MonsterRegistry.java:349`) is display-only.
- `DamageTypes` is not an enum (a `String[]` + English-alias map) and has no `label()` to fix —
  skip, just grep for any paint site printing `damageAffinities` keys raw.
- **`Condition` is the hard case**: its enum constants themselves are Spanish
  (`CEGADO`, `HECHIZADO`, ...) and `label() = name().toLowerCase()` doubles as the
  persisted/networked value (`Combatant.java:406-426`, `Condition.fromLabel` parsed back at
  `Combatant.java:674`, `SheetCommand.java:302`, `TurnManager.java:836,852`,
  `ConditionListScreen.java:41`, sent over network via `BrowseActionMessage.java:517`,
  `SheetSummaryRequestMessage.java:57`). **Do not rename the enum constants or change what
  `fromLabel`/storage reads** — this is persisted player data, not command syntax the user
  agreed to break. Instead: add a separate English `displayLabel()` (ordinal-indexed array,
  same pattern `MagicSchool`/`CreatureType` already use for their alias arrays) and route every
  UI/chat call site to it, while `fromLabel` keeps accepting the existing Spanish tokens.

**Verify:** `gradlew testJsonContent`; specifically confirm the unrelated `label()` methods on
save-DC records (`MonsterActionManager.java:487`, `SpellCastManager.java:626`) aren't caught by
a broad find/replace. Grep-for-Spanish sweep across the 4 files post-edit. If
`checkNetworkShape`/`checkNetworkWire` fails, follow the hash re-pin + `PROTOCOL_VERSION` bump
process from project memory — expected not to trigger by this design, but the one place it could.

### Phase 6 — `presets.json` class/subclass names (24 raw Spanish names)
Per the grounded research: `SpellSlots.casterFor`, `Config.hitDieFor`, and
`Config.WeaponDefault.allowsClass` already substring-match **both** English and Spanish class
names — so translating the preset names does not require the full id-based decoupling the old
`content_lang_keys.py` comment worried about.

1. Translate `presets.json`'s 24 `"name"` fields directly to English literal text
   (`Guerrero`→`Fighter`, `Escuela de Evocación`→`School of Evocation`, etc.) via targeted text
   substitution (anchor on `"id"` boundaries, replace only the `"name": "..."` value) — matching
   the existing raw-text convention (no translation key, same as `feats.json` descriptions).
2. No Java changes needed at the write site: `PresetRegistry.java:134-135` already writes
   `preset.name()` straight from the parsed JSON — new characters get English automatically.
3. **Leave already-saved characters alone** — their `characterClass`/`characterSubclass` text
   stays whatever was written when the preset was applied (same non-goal as the existing
   en/es lang-key system, which never rewrites existing player data). The substring matchers
   keep matching old Spanish saves since their Spanish substrings remain in the match lists.
4. Update `content_lang_keys.py`'s exclusion comment (`tools/content_lang_keys.py:30-36`) to
   note presets.json was handled via direct translation, not key migration, so a future
   contributor doesn't re-attempt the id-based redesign it currently describes as "the fix."
5. If Phase 4's `CharacterOptionsRegistry.java` check turns up a class/race/background list
   separate from `presets.json`, apply the same direct swap there too.

**Verify:** `gradlew testJsonContent`; manual grep of `presets.json` for remaining accented
chars; sanity-check a save/load round trip (create character, apply a preset, reload sheet).

### Phase 7 — Java comments (269 of 284 files)
Don't enumerate files by hand. Mechanical batch sweep:
1. Generate the worklist: `git ls-files -- '*.java'` filtered by the same
   `[áéíóúñÁÉÍÓÚÑ¿¡]` pattern the self-tests already use.
2. Partition into batches of ~15-25 files, never straddling a module boundary
   (`src/main`, `dungeon/`, `species/`, and each module's `src/test` are separate batch groups).
3. Dispatch each batch (subagent or sequential turns) with a narrow brief: translate only

   translate meaning, not word-for-word), don't touch string literals/identifiers/logic,
   preserve `{@code}`/`{@link}`/HTML tags inside Javadoc verbatim.
4. Since comments are behaviorally inert, don't gate every batch on a full build — run
   `gradlew build` once after all batches (or every few), and treat the real verification as a
   final `[áéíóúñÁÉÍÓÚÑ¿¡]` grep outside string literals returning zero, module by module.
5. Can run in parallel with Phases 1-6 on files those phases don't touch, to avoid merge noise;
   handle files that overlap with earlier phases last.

### Phase 8 — Self-test assertion messages
Files: `JsonContentSelfTest.java` (1,135 occurrences, by far the largest — do last, after Phases
1-6 have already made their required edits to this same file, e.g. the `enComandos` cap change),
`dungeon/.../DungeonSelfTest.java`, `species/.../SpeciesSelfTest.java`. Translate
`assertTrue(..., "message")` and diagnostic `println` strings only — behavior-preserving, no
assertion-condition changes. Watch the `SPANISH_VARIANTS = {...}` block `sync_lang_variants.py:18`
regex-parses — don't reflow it across lines while editing nearby text.
**Verify:** `gradlew build` passing before and after (same assertions, translated text) is the
practical proof; diff review to confirm no condition was accidentally altered.

### Phase 9 — Dev-only test fixtures (`test/dndsheets/*/ejemplo.json`)
Lowest priority, not shipped. Translate embedded Spanish example content. Check first whether
any self-test hand-parses these expecting specific Spanish strings.

## Verification (end to end)
1. After each phase: `cmd /c "gradlew build 2>&1"` (or `testJsonContent` for lang-only phases).
2. After Phase 7 completes: full-tree grep for `[áéíóúñÁÉÍÓÚÑ¿¡]` outside string literals in

## Context

The mod is currently a mix of English and Spanish across almost every layer — not just the
translation files. Three exploration passes over the repo found:

- `lang/en_us.json` (main mod) is 99.7% clean English — only 5 keys leak Spanish menu-name
  references.
- The Java source is **overwhelmingly Spanish**: 269 of 284 `.java` files contain Spanish text
  (comments and/or string literals), 6,277 accented-character occurrences total. Chat/command
  feedback built with `Component.literal("...")` (which bypasses the translation system
  entirely) is Spanish in ~30 places across ~20 files — this is what a player/DM actually sees
  mid-session and is the most likely trigger for "the mod is only partially translated."
- Command-tree argument names and one subcommand (`/dndchar mejora`) are Spanish words, visible
  in tab-completion and usage syntax.
- Two content JSON files (`feats.json`, `presets.json`) embed raw Spanish prose/names with no
  translation key at all — `presets.json` is a known hard case (see below).
- Enum `label()` methods (`MagicSchool`, `CreatureType`, `CreatureSize`, `Condition`) bake
  Spanish display text into Java, separate from the intentionally-Spanish internal storage keys.
- The user confirmed scope is **everything**, including developer-only Java comments and
  self-test assertion messages, and confirmed Spanish command literals/arguments should be
  **renamed cleanly with no backward-compat aliases**.

The one genuinely hard case is `presets.json`'s 24 class/subclass names: a project memory
(confirmed by reading `tools/content_lang_keys.py:30-36`, which deliberately excludes this file)
says the preset name is **written directly** into the sheet's free-text `characterClass` field,
and `SpellSlots.casterFor` used to be described as deducing spellcasting by substring-matching
that text. Reading the actual code shows this is **already bilingual-tolerant**
(`SpellSlots.java:52-79`, `Config.hitDieFor`, `Config.WeaponDefault.allowsClass` all match
English *and* Spanish substrings already), which substantially de-risks this phase versus a
from-scratch id-based redesign — see Phase 6.

Goal: every layer of the mod — player-facing text, command syntax, content data, enum display
labels, hardcoded registry names, Java comments, and self-test messages — ends up in English,
without breaking the existing self-test suite (`gradlew build`, 3 test suites, 60+ checks) or
silently corrupting already-saved player data (`Condition` is the one place persisted data is at
stake).

## Verification tools available (from project memory + confirmed in code)

- `gradlew build` runs all 3 self-tests without a Forge runtime; `gradlew testJsonContent` runs
  just the core one. No Gradle daemon on this machine — cold build ~25-35s. **Capture stderr**:
  `cmd /c "gradlew build 2>&1"` (PowerShell alone drops `AssertionError` output).
  Note: this repo is normally driven from PowerShell — use the `cmd /c "... 2>&1"` wrapper form
  shown above rather than bash-style redirection.
- `checkChatMessagesAreTranslatable` (`JsonContentSelfTest.java:~3483-3557`) already fails the
  build on stray prose `Component.literal(...)` outside `/command/` files, and tracks a counter
  `enComandos` of tolerated command-file literals, capped `<= 86` with a `ponytail:` comment
  saying explicitly this cap exists so the count doesn't grow, and "lowering it to 0 is the
  batch that's missing" — confirmed at `JsonContentSelfTest.java:3495-3507`. Phase 2 is that
  missing batch; **lower the cap as literals are converted, don't leave it at 86**.
  - Reading it more closely: this check does not need blanket exemption or restructuring — its
    file/dir partitioning (`/command/` vs. elsewhere) already matches this plan's phase
    boundaries. No changes to the check's *logic* are needed, only to the cap constant as Phase
    2 converts literals.
- `checkTranslationKeysExist` catches any `Component.translatable("key")` used in code without a
  matching `en_us.json` entry.
- `checkContentNamesAreTranslated` is the established pattern for content-name-as-key (used for
  spells/monsters/items/weapons); `presets.json` was deliberately excluded — Phase 6 keeps it
  excluded (see design below) rather than extending this check.
- Visible-text convention: edit `en_us.json` **and** `es_es.json` (alphabetical order), then run
  `python tools/sync_lang_variants.py` to propagate to the other 6 `es_*` variants.
  `sync_lang_variants.py:18` regex-parses a `SPANISH_VARIANTS = {...}` block out of
  `JsonContentSelfTest.java` — don't reflow that declaration across lines while editing nearby
  text (relevant to Phase 8).
- Content pack JSON (`src/main/resources/dndsheets/defaults/*.json`) is hand-formatted, ~14,000
  lines total — edit with targeted text substitution (same approach as `tools/content_lang_keys.py`),
  never a full JSON parse+dump, or unrelated lines reflow.
- No network/protocol changes are expected anywhere in this plan except possibly `Condition`
  (Phase 5) — if `checkNetworkShape`/`checkNetworkWire` fails there, it prints the new hash to
  paste into `DndsheetsMod`'s `NETWORK_SHAPE`/`ORDER`/`WIRE` constants; bump `PROTOCOL_VERSION`
  and note why above it. Phase 5's design avoids touching the wire format on purpose, so this
  should not trigger, but is called out as the one checkpoint where it plausibly could.

## Phased plan

Ordered safest/most mechanical → most invasive, with the two persisted-data risks (`Condition`,
`presets.json`) sequenced back-to-back near the end of the code-behavior phases.

### Phase 0 — Baseline
Run `cmd /c "gradlew build 2>&1"` once before touching anything, to confirm a clean starting
point. No file changes.

### Phase 1 — `lang/en_us.json` cleanup (5 leaked keys)
Fix the Spanish text leaked into `chat.dndsheets.character.setup_hint`,
`gui.dndsheets.guide.page.skills` (2 spots), `gui.dndsheets.guide.page.subclass`. Two of the five
reference the literal command `/dndchar mejora` — **defer those two specific edits to land in
the same commit as Phase 3** (command rename), so this file isn't touched twice for the same
reason. Fix the other 3 now.
**Verify:** `gradlew testJsonContent`.

### Phase 2 — Hardcoded Spanish `Component.literal(...)` in chat/command feedback (~30 calls, ~20 files)
Files: `command/CharacterCommand.java`, `CharacterOptionsCommand.java`, `EncounterCommand.java`,
`PresetCommand.java`, `MagicItemCommand.java`, `MonsterCommand.java`, `WeaponCommand.java`,
`TraitCommand.java`, `SpellCommand.java`, `SheetCommand.java`, `ContentCommands.java`,
`RollLogCommand.java`, `JournalCommand.java`, `TurnCommand.java`,
`dungeon/.../command/DungeonCommand.java`, `ChatFeedback.java`, `CharacterSetupScreen.java`,
`GuideBook.java`, `NameTagHp.java`, `network/CharacterSheetOpenMessage.java`,
`client/gui/CharacterSheetScreen.java:999`, `dungeon/.../DungeonTraceScreen.java`.

Convert each `Component.literal("...Spanish...")` to `Component.translatable(key, args...)`,
add the key to `en_us.json` **and** `es_es.json` (English text in en_us, the original Spanish
prose moved into es_es as its value), then `python tools/sync_lang_variants.py`.

**Verify:** `gradlew testJsonContent` — watch `enComandos` in
`checkChatMessagesAreTranslatable` drop as literals convert; **lower the `<= 86` cap
(`JsonContentSelfTest.java:3506`) to match the new true count** once done (ideally 0). Manual
grep for remaining `Component.literal("` with accented chars under `/command/` afterward, since
the self-test only fails on cap breach, not on nonzero count.

### Phase 3 — Command tree rename (breaking, no aliases — per user decision)
`Commands.literal("mejora")` → `"improve"` (`CharacterCommand.java`). Argument names:
`"nombre"→"name"`, `"categoria"→"category"`, `"objetivo"→"target"`, `"cantidad"→"amount"`,
`"jugador"→"player"`, `"clase"→"class"`, `"nivel"→"level"`, `"valor"→"value"`, `"tipo"→"type"`
across `CharacterCommand.java`, `CharacterOptionsCommand.java`, `DistanceCommand.java`,
`RollLogCommand.java`, `MonsterCommand.java`, `SheetCommand.java`, `WeaponCommand.java`,
`TurnCommand.java`. Every `context.getArgument("nombre", ...)` call site in the same file must
change in lockstep with its declaration — a missed one is a compile error, which is self-checking.
Do this **after** Phase 1/2 so no lang key or chat message still references the old command
name once it's gone; grep lang files and all `Component.literal`/`translatable` string
arguments for `mejora` afterward as a final check.
**Verify:** `gradlew build` (compile failure catches missed rename sites).

### Phase 4 — Species submodule hardcoded Spanish names
Files: `species/src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/species/RaceRegistry.java`,
`BackgroundRegistry.java`, `DndsheetsSpeciesMod.java`.

These are the **fallback-only picker path** (used only when the Origins addon isn't installed —
the primary Origins-driven path already has full 8-language support via
`dndsheets_species/lang/*.json`, unrelated to this fix). Direct literal swap, not a new key
system — reuse the exact English wording already present in `origin.dndsheets_species.<id>.name`
lang keys for the same ids where they exist (e.g. `"acolyte"` → `"Acolyte"`), so the two paths
stay consistent. Also translate `RaceRegistry.java`'s Spanish description string(s) directly (raw
text, same convention as `items.json`/`feats.json` descriptions — not keyed).

Also check `CharacterOptionsRegistry.java` (the core-mod equivalent fallback picker source) for
the same hardcoded-Spanish-names pattern — confirm during implementation whether it's a separate
source from `PresetRegistry`/`presets.json`, and if so apply the same swap.

**Verify:** `gradlew build`; check `species/src/test/.../SpeciesSelfTest.java` for any assertion
on exact Spanish strings and update it in the same commit if found. Manual grep for remaining
accented chars in the touched files.

### Phase 5 — Enum `label()` display text
Files: `MagicSchool.java`, `CreatureType.java`, `CreatureSize.java`, `Condition.java`.

- `MagicSchool`/`CreatureType`: change only the `label()` switch bodies to English — the
  internal Spanish `key`/English-alias arrays used for JSON parsing stay untouched (storage
  format, not display). Confirm the paint sites (`SpellRegistry.java:226`,
  `MonsterRegistry.java:348-349`) write into display-only JSON output, not something re-parsed
  expecting the Spanish form.
- `CreatureSize.label()` currently returns the Spanish `key` verbatim (no separate switch) —
  add one, after confirming its only consumer (`MonsterRegistry.java:349`) is display-only.
- `DamageTypes` is not an enum (a `String[]` + English-alias map) and has no `label()` to fix —
  skip, just grep for any paint site printing `damageAffinities` keys raw.
- **`Condition` is the hard case**: its enum constants themselves are Spanish
  (`CEGADO`, `HECHIZADO`, ...) and `label() = name().toLowerCase()` doubles as the
  persisted/networked value (`Combatant.java:406-426`, `Condition.fromLabel` parsed back at
  `Combatant.java:674`, `SheetCommand.java:302`, `TurnManager.java:836,852`,
  `ConditionListScreen.java:41`, sent over network via `BrowseActionMessage.java:517`,
  `SheetSummaryRequestMessage.java:57`). **Do not rename the enum constants or change what
  `fromLabel`/storage reads** — this is persisted player data, not command syntax the user
  agreed to break. Instead: add a separate English `displayLabel()` (ordinal-indexed array,
  same pattern `MagicSchool`/`CreatureType` already use for their alias arrays) and route every
  UI/chat call site to it, while `fromLabel` keeps accepting the existing Spanish tokens.

**Verify:** `gradlew testJsonContent`; specifically confirm the unrelated `label()` methods on
save-DC records (`MonsterActionManager.java:487`, `SpellCastManager.java:626`) aren't caught by
a broad find/replace. Grep-for-Spanish sweep across the 4 files post-edit. If
`checkNetworkShape`/`checkNetworkWire` fails, follow the hash re-pin + `PROTOCOL_VERSION` bump
process from project memory — expected not to trigger by this design, but the one place it could.

### Phase 6 — `presets.json` class/subclass names (24 raw Spanish names)
Per the grounded research: `SpellSlots.casterFor`, `Config.hitDieFor`, and
`Config.WeaponDefault.allowsClass` already substring-match **both** English and Spanish class
names — so translating the preset names does not require the full id-based decoupling the old
`content_lang_keys.py` comment worried about.

1. Translate `presets.json`'s 24 `"name"` fields directly to English literal text
   (`Guerrero`→`Fighter`, `Escuela de Evocación`→`School of Evocation`, etc.) via targeted text
   substitution (anchor on `"id"` boundaries, replace only the `"name": "..."` value) — matching
   the existing raw-text convention (no translation key, same as `feats.json` descriptions).
2. No Java changes needed at the write site: `PresetRegistry.java:134-135` already writes
   `preset.name()` straight from the parsed JSON — new characters get English automatically.
3. **Leave already-saved characters alone** — their `characterClass`/`characterSubclass` text
   stays whatever was written when the preset was applied (same non-goal as the existing
   en/es lang-key system, which never rewrites existing player data). The substring matchers
   keep matching old Spanish saves since their Spanish substrings remain in the match lists.
4. Update `content_lang_keys.py`'s exclusion comment (`tools/content_lang_keys.py:30-36`) to
   note presets.json was handled via direct translation, not key migration, so a future
   contributor doesn't re-attempt the id-based redesign it currently describes as "the fix."
5. If Phase 4's `CharacterOptionsRegistry.java` check turns up a class/race/background list
   separate from `presets.json`, apply the same direct swap there too.

**Verify:** `gradlew testJsonContent`; manual grep of `presets.json` for remaining accented
chars; sanity-check a save/load round trip (create character, apply a preset, reload sheet).

### Phase 7 — Java comments (269 of 284 files)
Don't enumerate files by hand. Mechanical batch sweep:
1. Generate the worklist: `git ls-files -- '*.java'` filtered by the same
   `[áéíóúñÁÉÍÓÚÑ¿¡]` pattern the self-tests already use.
2. Partition into batches of ~15-25 files, never straddling a module boundary
   (`src/main`, `dungeon/`, `species/`, and each module's `src/test` are separate batch groups).
3. Dispatch each batch (subagent or sequential turns) with a narrow brief: translate only
   Javadoc/`//` comments from Spanish to English, preserve technical precision (many comments
   carry load-bearing rationale — e.g. the exact `presets.json` exclusion note found above —
   translate meaning, not word-for-word), don't touch string literals/identifiers/logic,
   preserve `{@code}`/`{@link}`/HTML tags inside Javadoc verbatim.
4. Since comments are behaviorally inert, don't gate every batch on a full build — run
   `gradlew build` once after all batches (or every few), and treat the real verification as a
   final `[áéíóúñÁÉÍÓÚÑ¿¡]` grep outside string literals returning zero, module by module.
5. Can run in parallel with Phases 1-6 on files those phases don't touch, to avoid merge noise;
   handle files that overlap with earlier phases last.

### Phase 8 — Self-test assertion messages
Files: `JsonContentSelfTest.java` (1,135 occurrences, by far the largest — do last, after Phases
1-6 have already made their required edits to this same file, e.g. the `enComandos` cap change),
`dungeon/.../DungeonSelfTest.java`, `species/.../SpeciesSelfTest.java`. Translate
`assertTrue(..., "message")` and diagnostic `println` strings only — behavior-preserving, no
assertion-condition changes. Watch the `SPANISH_VARIANTS = {...}` block `sync_lang_variants.py:18`
regex-parses — don't reflow it across lines while editing nearby text.
**Verify:** `gradlew build` passing before and after (same assertions, translated text) is the
practical proof; diff review to confirm no condition was accidentally altered.

### Phase 9 — Dev-only test fixtures (`test/dndsheets/*/ejemplo.json`)
Lowest priority, not shipped. Translate embedded Spanish example content. Check first whether
any self-test hand-parses these expecting specific Spanish strings.

## Verification (end to end)
1. After each phase: `cmd /c "gradlew build 2>&1"` (or `testJsonContent` for lang-only phases).
2. After Phase 7 completes: full-tree grep for `[áéíóúñÁÉÍÓÚÑ¿¡]` outside string literals in
   `.java` files, module by module, expect zero.
3. After Phase 2/8: confirm the `enComandos` cap in `JsonContentSelfTest.java` reflects reality
   (ideally 0), not left at the old `86`.
4. Manual save/load round-trip test for Phase 5 (`Condition`) and Phase 6 (`presets.json`) since
   these touch persisted player data — create a character, apply a preset, add a condition,
   reload the sheet, confirm no raw translation key or broken text appears anywhere.
5. `runClient` doesn't load `dungeon`/`species` addons — verifying those modules' in-game text
   (command tab-completion, GUI labels) requires installing the real jar from `gradlew build`.

- Visible-text convention: edit `en_us.json` **and** `es_es.json` (alphabetical order), then run
  `python tools/sync_lang_variants.py` to propagate to the other 6 `es_*` variants.
  `sync_lang_variants.py:18` regex-parses a `SPANISH_VARIANTS = {...}` block out of
  `JsonContentSelfTest.java` — don't reflow that declaration across lines while editing nearby
  text (relevant to Phase 8).
- Content pack JSON (`src/main/resources/dndsheets/defaults/*.json`) is hand-formatted, ~14,000
  lines total — edit with targeted text substitution (same approach as `tools/content_lang_keys.py`),
  never a full JSON parse+dump, or unrelated lines reflow.
- No network/protocol changes are expected anywhere in this plan except possibly `Condition`
  (Phase 5) — if `checkNetworkShape`/`checkNetworkWire` fails there, it prints the new hash to
  paste into `DndsheetsMod`'s `NETWORK_SHAPE`/`ORDER`/`WIRE` constants; bump `PROTOCOL_VERSION`
  and note why above it. Phase 5's design avoids touching the wire format on purpose, so this
  should not trigger, but is called out as the one checkpoint where it plausibly could.

## Phased plan

Ordered safest/most mechanical → most invasive, with the two persisted-data risks (`Condition`,
`presets.json`) sequenced back-to-back near the end of the code-behavior phases.

### Phase 0 — Baseline
Run `cmd /c "gradlew build 2>&1"` once before touching anything, to confirm a clean starting
point. No file changes.

### Phase 1 — `lang/en_us.json` cleanup (5 leaked keys)
Fix the Spanish text leaked into `chat.dndsheets.character.setup_hint`,
`gui.dndsheets.guide.page.skills` (2 spots), `gui.dndsheets.guide.page.subclass`. Two of the five
reference the literal command `/dndchar mejora` — **defer those two specific edits to land in
the same commit as Phase 3** (command rename), so this file isn't touched twice for the same
reason. Fix the other 3 now.
**Verify:** `gradlew testJsonContent`.

### Phase 2 — Hardcoded Spanish `Component.literal(...)` in chat/command feedback (~30 calls, ~20 files)
Files: `command/CharacterCommand.java`, `CharacterOptionsCommand.java`, `EncounterCommand.java`,
`PresetCommand.java`, `MagicItemCommand.java`, `MonsterCommand.java`, `WeaponCommand.java`,
`TraitCommand.java`, `SpellCommand.java`, `SheetCommand.java`, `ContentCommands.java`,
`RollLogCommand.java`, `JournalCommand.java`, `TurnCommand.java`,
`dungeon/.../command/DungeonCommand.java`, `ChatFeedback.java`, `CharacterSetupScreen.java`,
`GuideBook.java`, `NameTagHp.java`, `network/CharacterSheetOpenMessage.java`,
`client/gui/CharacterSheetScreen.java:999`, `dungeon/.../DungeonTraceScreen.java`.

Convert each `Component.literal("...Spanish...")` to `Component.translatable(key, args...)`,
add the key to `en_us.json` **and** `es_es.json` (English text in en_us, the original Spanish
prose moved into es_es as its value), then `python tools/sync_lang_variants.py`.

**Verify:** `gradlew testJsonContent` — watch `enComandos` in
`checkChatMessagesAreTranslatable` drop as literals convert; **lower the `<= 86` cap
(`JsonContentSelfTest.java:3506`) to match the new true count** once done (ideally 0). Manual
grep for remaining `Component.literal("` with accented chars under `/command/` afterward, since
the self-test only fails on cap breach, not on nonzero count.

### Phase 3 — Command tree rename (breaking, no aliases — per user decision)
`Commands.literal("mejora")` → `"improve"` (`CharacterCommand.java`). Argument names:
`"nombre"→"name"`, `"categoria"→"category"`, `"objetivo"→"target"`, `"cantidad"→"amount"`,
`"jugador"→"player"`, `"clase"→"class"`, `"nivel"→"level"`, `"valor"→"value"`, `"tipo"→"type"`
across `CharacterCommand.java`, `CharacterOptionsCommand.java`, `DistanceCommand.java`,
`RollLogCommand.java`, `MonsterCommand.java`, `SheetCommand.java`, `WeaponCommand.java`,
`TurnCommand.java`. Every `context.getArgument("nombre", ...)` call site in the same file must
change in lockstep with its declaration — a missed one is a compile error, which is self-checking.
Do this **after** Phase 1/2 so no lang key or chat message still references the old command
name once it's gone; grep lang files and all `Component.literal`/`translatable` string
arguments for `mejora` afterward as a final check.
**Verify:** `gradlew build` (compile failure catches missed rename sites).

### Phase 4 — Species submodule hardcoded Spanish names
Files: `species/src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/species/RaceRegistry.java`,
`BackgroundRegistry.java`, `DndsheetsSpeciesMod.java`.

These are the **fallback-only picker path** (used only when the Origins addon isn't installed —
the primary Origins-driven path already has full 8-language support via
`dndsheets_species/lang/*.json`, unrelated to this fix). Direct literal swap, not a new key
system — reuse the exact English wording already present in `origin.dndsheets_species.<id>.name`
lang keys for the same ids where they exist (e.g. `"acolyte"` → `"Acolyte"`), so the two paths
stay consistent. Also translate `RaceRegistry.java`'s Spanish description string(s) directly (raw
text, same convention as `items.json`/`feats.json` descriptions — not keyed).

Also check `CharacterOptionsRegistry.java` (the core-mod equivalent fallback picker source) for
the same hardcoded-Spanish-names pattern — confirm during implementation whether it's a separate
source from `PresetRegistry`/`presets.json`, and if so apply the same swap.

**Verify:** `gradlew build`; check `species/src/test/.../SpeciesSelfTest.java` for any assertion
on exact Spanish strings and update it in the same commit if found. Manual grep for remaining
accented chars in the touched files.

### Phase 5 — Enum `label()` display text
Files: `MagicSchool.java`, `CreatureType.java`, `CreatureSize.java`, `Condition.java`.

- `MagicSchool`/`CreatureType`: change only the `label()` switch bodies to English — the
  internal Spanish `key`/English-alias arrays used for JSON parsing stay untouched (storage
  format, not display). Confirm the paint sites (`SpellRegistry.java:226`,
  `MonsterRegistry.java:348-349`) write into display-only JSON output, not something re-parsed
  expecting the Spanish form.
- `CreatureSize.label()` currently returns the Spanish `key` verbatim (no separate switch) —
  add one, after confirming its only consumer (`MonsterRegistry.java:349`) is display-only.
- `DamageTypes` is not an enum (a `String[]` + English-alias map) and has no `label()` to fix —
  skip, just grep for any paint site printing `damageAffinities` keys raw.
- **`Condition` is the hard case**: its enum constants themselves are Spanish
  (`CEGADO`, `HECHIZADO`, ...) and `label() = name().toLowerCase()` doubles as the
  persisted/networked value (`Combatant.java:406-426`, `Condition.fromLabel` parsed back at
  `Combatant.java:674`, `SheetCommand.java:302`, `TurnManager.java:836,852`,
  `ConditionListScreen.java:41`, sent over network via `BrowseActionMessage.java:517`,
  `SheetSummaryRequestMessage.java:57`). **Do not rename the enum constants or change what
  `fromLabel`/storage reads** — this is persisted player data, not command syntax the user
  agreed to break. Instead: add a separate English `displayLabel()` (ordinal-indexed array,
  same pattern `MagicSchool`/`CreatureType` already use for their alias arrays) and route every
  UI/chat call site to it, while `fromLabel` keeps accepting the existing Spanish tokens.

**Verify:** `gradlew testJsonContent`; specifically confirm the unrelated `label()` methods on
save-DC records (`MonsterActionManager.java:487`, `SpellCastManager.java:626`) aren't caught by
a broad find/replace. Grep-for-Spanish sweep across the 4 files post-edit. If
`checkNetworkShape`/`checkNetworkWire` fails, follow the hash re-pin + `PROTOCOL_VERSION` bump
process from project memory — expected not to trigger by this design, but the one place it could.

### Phase 6 — `presets.json` class/subclass names (24 raw Spanish names)
Per the grounded research: `SpellSlots.casterFor`, `Config.hitDieFor`, and
`Config.WeaponDefault.allowsClass` already substring-match **both** English and Spanish class
names — so translating the preset names does not require the full id-based decoupling the old
`content_lang_keys.py` comment worried about.

1. Translate `presets.json`'s 24 `"name"` fields directly to English literal text
   (`Guerrero`→`Fighter`, `Escuela de Evocación`→`School of Evocation`, etc.) via targeted text
   substitution (anchor on `"id"` boundaries, replace only the `"name": "..."` value) — matching
   the existing raw-text convention (no translation key, same as `feats.json` descriptions).
2. No Java changes needed at the write site: `PresetRegistry.java:134-135` already writes
   `preset.name()` straight from the parsed JSON — new characters get English automatically.
3. **Leave already-saved characters alone** — their `characterClass`/`characterSubclass` text
   stays whatever was written when the preset was applied (same non-goal as the existing
   en/es lang-key system, which never rewrites existing player data). The substring matchers
   keep matching old Spanish saves since their Spanish substrings remain in the match lists.
4. Update `content_lang_keys.py`'s exclusion comment (`tools/content_lang_keys.py:30-36`) to
   note presets.json was handled via direct translation, not key migration, so a future
   contributor doesn't re-attempt the id-based redesign it currently describes as "the fix."
5. If Phase 4's `CharacterOptionsRegistry.java` check turns up a class/race/background list
   separate from `presets.json`, apply the same direct swap there too.

**Verify:** `gradlew testJsonContent`; manual grep of `presets.json` for remaining accented
chars; sanity-check a save/load round trip (create character, apply a preset, reload sheet).

### Phase 7 — Java comments (269 of 284 files)
Don't enumerate files by hand. Mechanical batch sweep:
1. Generate the worklist: `git ls-files -- '*.java'` filtered by the same
   `[áéíóúñÁÉÍÓÚÑ¿¡]` pattern the self-tests already use.
2. Partition into batches of ~15-25 files, never straddling a module boundary
   (`src/main`, `dungeon/`, `species/`, and each module's `src/test` are separate batch groups).
3. Dispatch each batch (subagent or sequential turns) with a narrow brief: translate only
   Javadoc/`//` comments from Spanish to English, preserve technical precision (many comments
   carry load-bearing rationale — e.g. the exact `presets.json` exclusion note found above —
   translate meaning, not word-for-word), don't touch string literals/identifiers/logic,
   preserve `{@code}`/`{@link}`/HTML tags inside Javadoc verbatim.
4. Since comments are behaviorally inert, don't gate every batch on a full build — run
   `gradlew build` once after all batches (or every few), and treat the real verification as a
   final `[áéíóúñÁÉÍÓÚÑ¿¡]` grep outside string literals returning zero, module by module.
5. Can run in parallel with Phases 1-6 on files those phases don't touch, to avoid merge noise;
   handle files that overlap with earlier phases last.

### Phase 8 — Self-test assertion messages
Files: `JsonContentSelfTest.java` (1,135 occurrences, by far the largest — do last, after Phases
1-6 have already made their required edits to this same file, e.g. the `enComandos` cap change),
`dungeon/.../DungeonSelfTest.java`, `species/.../SpeciesSelfTest.java`. Translate
`assertTrue(..., "message")` and diagnostic `println` strings only — behavior-preserving, no
assertion-condition changes. Watch the `SPANISH_VARIANTS = {...}` block `sync_lang_variants.py:18`
regex-parses — don't reflow it across lines while editing nearby text.
**Verify:** `gradlew build` passing before and after (same assertions, translated text) is the
practical proof; diff review to confirm no condition was accidentally altered.

### Phase 9 — Dev-only test fixtures (`test/dndsheets/*/ejemplo.json`)
Lowest priority, not shipped. Translate embedded Spanish example content. Check first whether
any self-test hand-parses these expecting specific Spanish strings.

## Verification (end to end)
1. After each phase: `cmd /c "gradlew build 2>&1"` (or `testJsonContent` for lang-only phases).
2. After Phase 7 completes: full-tree grep for `[áéíóúñÁÉÍÓÚÑ¿¡]` outside string literals in
   `.java` files, module by module, expect zero.
3. After Phase 2/8: confirm the `enComandos` cap in `JsonContentSelfTest.java` reflects reality
   (ideally 0), not left at the old `86`.
4. Manual save/load round-trip test for Phase 5 (`Condition`) and Phase 6 (`presets.json`) since
   these touch persisted player data — create a character, apply a preset, add a condition,
   reload the sheet, confirm no raw translation key or broken text appears anywhere.
5. `runClient` doesn't load `dungeon`/`species` addons — verifying those modules' in-game text
   (command tab-completion, GUI labels) requires installing the real jar from `gradlew build`.

entries.name: ExitPlanMode
entries.description:
Use this tool when you are in plan mode and have finished writing your plan to the plan file and are ready for user approval.

## How This Tool Works
- You should have already written your plan to the plan file specified in the plan mode system message
- This tool does NOT take the plan content as a parameter - it will read the plan from the file you wrote
- This tool simply signals that you're done planning and ready for the user to review and approve
- The user will see the contents of your plan file when they review it

## When to Use This Tool
IMPORTANT: Only use this tool when the task requires planning the implementation steps of a task that requires writing code. For research tasks where you're gathering information, searching files, reading files or in general trying to understand the codebase - do NOT use this tool.

## Before Using This Tool
Ensure your plan is complete and unambiguous:
- If you have unresolved questions about requirements or approach, use AskUserQuestion first (in earlier phases)
- Once your plan is finalized, use THIS tool to request approval

**Important:** Do NOT use AskUserQuestion to ask "Is this plan okay?" or "Should I proceed?" - that's exactly what THIS tool does. ExitPlanMode inherently requests user approval of your plan.

## Examples

1. Initial task: "Search for and understand the implementation of vim mode in the codebase" - Do not use the exit plan mode tool because you are not planning the implementation steps of a task.
2. Initial task: "Help me implement yank mode for vim" - Use the exit plan mode tool after you have finished planning the implementation steps of the task.
3. Initial task: "Add a new feature to handle user authentication" - If unsure about auth method (OAuth, JWT, etc.), use AskUserQuestion first, then use exit plan mode tool after clarifying the approach.

input.description: Translate species registry hardcoded Spanish names
input.prompt:
Repo: C:\Users\DanCastello\Documents\GitHub\dndsheets — a Minecraft Forge 1.20.1 mod (Java, multi-module). We're translating the whole mod to English. This is Phase 4 of a 9-phase plan (full plan at C:\Users\DanCastello\.claude\plans\problem-the-mod-is-async-stroustrup.md for context, but this task is self-contained). Another agent is concurrently working on Phase 2 (command/chat feedback strings) in `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/command/*.java` and a few GUI/network files — DO NOT touch any file under `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/command/`, `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/client/`, or `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/network/` to avoid collision. Your scope is entirely within the `species/` module plus one file check in the root module described below.

## Background
`species/src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/species/RaceRegistry.java`, `BackgroundRegistry.java`, and `DndsheetsSpeciesMod.java` hardcode Spanish display names and descriptions directly in Java constructors — e.g. `new Race("dragonborn", "Dracónido", ...)`, `new Background("acolyte", "Acólito", ...)`, `trait("fey_ancestry", "Ascendencia Feérica")`. These are NOT sourced from any lang file. This is deliberately a **fallback-only picker path**: it's only used in-game when the Origins addon mod isn't installed. When Origins IS installed, a separate, already-fully-English, already-multi-language system takes over instead (`species/src/main/resources/assets/dndsheets_species/lang/*.json`, using keys like `origin.dndsheets_species.<id>.name` / `.description` — already 100% clean English with a full 8-language set, not your concern, don't touch it).

## Task
1. Read `RaceRegistry.java`, `BackgroundRegistry.java`, `DndsheetsSpeciesMod.java` in full.
2. For every hardcoded Spanish display name (race names, background names, trait names) and any hardcoded Spanish description strings (e.g. a race description string in `RaceRegistry.java` mentioned in prior research), replace them with direct English literal text — NOT a translation key, just swap the literal string. This matches this fallback path's existing convention (never keyed) and avoids building new i18n infrastructure for a path that was never localized to begin with.
3. **Reuse exact existing English wording where it overlaps**: the `dndsheets_species/lang/en_us.json` file already has English names for the same ids via `origin.dndsheets_species.<id>.name` keys (e.g. `"acolyte"` → `"Acolyte"`). Where a Spanish name in `RaceRegistry`/`BackgroundRegistry`/`DndsheetsSpeciesMod` corresponds to the same id as an existing `origin.dndsheets_species.*` key, use that exact English wording (read the lang file first to get the precise strings) so both paths stay consistent. For anything without a matching lang key (e.g. description prose, or a trait/race id that has no origin-layer equivalent), translate it yourself to natural, accurate English (these are D&D 5e SRD race/background/trait names — use standard D&D 5e English terminology: e.g. "Dracónido"→"Dragonborn", "Ascendencia Feérica"→"Fey Ancestry", "Conocimiento Pétreo"→"Stonecunning", "Héroe del pueblo"→"Folk Hero", "Ermitaño"→"Hermit", etc. — these are standard SRD terms, get them exactly right).
4. Also check `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/CharacterOptionsRegistry.java` (root module, NOT the species module — this is the core-mod's own equivalent fallback picker source, separate from `species/`) for the same hardcoded-Spanish-names pattern. If it has hardcoded Spanish race/background/class option names, apply the same direct-literal-swap treatment there too, reusing the same English wording decisions you made above for matching ids.
5. Check `species/src/test/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/species/SpeciesSelfTest.java` for any assertion that checks an exact Spanish string value from these registries (e.g. `assertEquals("Dracónido", ...)`). If you find one, update it in the same pass to expect the new English value — don't leave a test asserting stale Spanish text.

## Verify
Run from repo root via PowerShell: `.\gradlew.bat build 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 150` (no Gradle daemon on this machine, expect a real compile+test run, allow a couple minutes). Confirm it passes. Then do a final grep for `[ñáéíóúÁÉÍÓÚÑ¿¡]` across `RaceRegistry.java`, `BackgroundRegistry.java`, `DndsheetsSpeciesMod.java`, and `CharacterOptionsRegistry.java` (if you touched it) to confirm no Spanish characters remain in string literals (Spanish in comments is fine — that's a different phase, not yours; only fix comments if trivially in the same line you're already touching, don't go out of your way for it).

## Report back
Concisely: which files you changed, how many names/strings translated, whether `CharacterOptionsRegistry.java` needed the same treatment, whether any self-test assertions needed updating, and confirm the build passes. This will be read by a coordinating agent, not the end user.

input.description: Translate enum label() display text to English
input.prompt:
Repo: C:\Users\DanCastello\Documents\GitHub\dndsheets — a Minecraft Forge 1.20.1 mod (Java). We're translating the whole mod to English. This is Phase 5 of a 9-phase plan (full plan at C:\Users\DanCastello\.claude\plans\problem-the-mod-is-async-stroustrup.md for context, but this task is self-contained). Other agents are concurrently working on: Phase 2 in `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/command/*.java` + a few `client/`/`network/` files, and Phase 4 in `species/` + `CharacterOptionsRegistry.java`. Your scope is exactly the 4 files named below — do not touch anything else, to avoid collisions.

## Background
Four classes in `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/`: `MagicSchool.java`, `CreatureType.java`, `CreatureSize.java`, `Condition.java`. These enums intentionally use **Spanish words as their internal canonical storage/JSON-parsing keys** (e.g. `MagicSchool`'s `key` field is `"evocacion"`) — that internal keying is NOT what you're changing, it's how content JSON round-trips and must keep working. What you ARE changing is only the **display label** text that players/DMs actually see in UI/chat/generated JSON output, which is currently hardcoded Spanish in each enum's `label()` method.

Read all 4 files in full before changing anything, plus these consumer sites to understand exactly what each `label()` call feeds: `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/SpellRegistry.java` (around line 226, writes `MagicSchool` label into pack JSON output), `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/MonsterRegistry.java` (around lines 348-349, writes `CreatureType`/`CreatureSize` labels into pack JSON/UI output), and grep the whole `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/` tree for `.label()` calls on these 4 types to find every consumer (there may be more than the two files named here — also check GUI screens, `ChatFeedback`, monster/spell display code).

## Task, per file

**`MagicSchool.java`**: change only the `label()` method's switch/if body strings to English (e.g. `"evocación"` → `"Evocation"`, and whatever the other ~4 Spanish-labeled entries are — translate each to its standard D&D 5e English school-of-magic name: Abjuration, Conjuration, Divination, Enchantment, Evocation, Illusion, Necromancy, Transmutation). Leave the enum constant names and the internal `key` field (used for JSON parsing/`parse()`) untouched — those stay Spanish, that's the storage format.

**`CreatureType.java`**: same pattern — change only `label()`'s Spanish-labeled entries (4 of 15) to standard D&D 5e English creature type names (e.g. whatever "humanoide" maps to → "Humanoid", etc. — use standard SRD terms: Aberration, Beast, Celestial, Construct, Dragon, Elemental, Fey, Fiend, Giant, Humanoid, Monstrosity, Ooze, Plant, Undead). Leave enum constants and internal `key` untouched.

**`CreatureSize.java`**: `label()` currently just returns the Spanish `key` verbatim with no separate switch. Add a proper `label()` implementation (switch/if, same shape as the other two enums) returning standard D&D 5e English size names (Tiny, Small, Medium, Large, Huge, Gargantuan — map from whatever Spanish `key` values exist, e.g. "gargantuesco"→"Gargantuan"). Leave `key`/`parse()` untouched. Before doing this, confirm via your grep that `CreatureSize.label()`'s only consumer(s) are display/output-only (not re-parsed elsewhere expecting the Spanish form) — if you find a consumer that re-parses the label output as if it were the storage key, flag it in your report instead of guessing.

**`Condition.java` — different treatment, read carefully:**
Do NOT rename the enum constants (`CEGADO`, `HECHIZADO`, `ENSORDECIDO`, etc.) and do NOT change what `Condition.fromLabel(String)` accepts or what gets written to persisted sheet JSON / sent over the network — this enum's `label()` (currently just `name().toLowerCase()`) doubles as the actual storage/network wire value for already-saved player data (conditions applied to existing characters, referenced in `Combatant.java`, `TurnManager.java`, `SheetCommand.java`, `BrowseActionMessage.java`, `SheetSummaryRequestMessage.java`, `ConditionListScreen.java` — grep for `Condition.fromLabel` and `.label()` calls on `Condition` to find every site). Renaming the stored value would corrupt already-saved games and require a network protocol bump.

Instead: **add a new method**, e.g. `displayLabel()`, that returns the English display name (Blinded, Charmed, Deafened, Frightened, Grappled, Incapacitated, Invisible, Paralyzed, Petrified, Poisoned, Prone, Restrained, Stunned, Unconscious, Exhaustion — standard D&D 5e SRD condition names, map each Spanish constant to its correct SRD English equivalent) via a switch on the enum constant (or an ordinal-indexed array, matching whatever style `MagicSchool`/`CreatureType` use for their similar alias arrays). input.description: Rename Spanish command literals and arguments to English
input.prompt:
Repo: C:\Users\DanCastello\Documents\GitHub\dndsheets — a Minecraft Forge 1.20.1 mod (Java, multi-module: root + `dungeon/` + `species/`). We're translating the whole mod to English. This is Phase 3 of a 9-phase plan (full plan at C:\Users\DanCastello\.claude\plans\problem-the-mod-is-async-stroustrup.md for context). Phases 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 9 are already done and merged into the working tree — a full `gradlew build` currently passes. This is a CLEAN BREAKING RENAME with no backward-compat aliases (explicitly decided by the user — do not add aliasing).

## Task
Rename Spanish Brigadier command literals/argument names to English across `src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/command/*.java` and `dungeon/src/main/java/net/hawthorn/dndsheets/dungeon/command/DungeonCommand.java`:

- `Commands.literal("mejora")` → `Commands.literal("improve")` (the `/dndchar mejora` ability-score-improvement subcommand, in `CharacterCommand.java`).
- Argument node names: `"nombre"→"name"`, `"categoria"→"category"`, `"objetivo"→"target"`, `"cantidad"→"amount"`, `"jugador"→"player"`, `"clase"→"class"`, `"nivel"→"level"`, `"valor"→"value"`, `"tipo"→"type"`.

Known files with these patterns: `CharacterCommand.java`, `CharacterOptionsCommand.java`, `DistanceCommand.java`, `RollLogCommand.java`, `MonsterCommand.java`, `SheetCommand.java`, `WeaponCommand.java`, `TurnCommand.java`. Also grep the whole `command/` directory and `DungeonCommand.java` for any `Commands.argument("<spanish-word>"` or `Commands.literal("<spanish-word>"` you find beyond this list — don't assume the list above is complete, verify by grepping for these exact strings and for other Spanish words in `Commands.literal(`/`Commands.argument(` calls specifically (not general string literals, just command-tree node names).

**Critical**: every `Commands.argument("nombre", ...)` declaration must be renamed in lockstep with every `context.getArgument("nombre", ...)` (or `StringArgumentType.getString(context, "nombre")`, `IntegerArgumentType.getInteger(context, "nombre")`, etc.) call site that reads that same argument, in the SAME file. A mismatch is a compile error — treat compile failure after your changes as the primary signal you missed a call site, and fix until `gradlew build` compiles clean. Some words like `"nivel"`/`"clase"`/`"tipo"` may appear as argument names in multiple different command files with different meanings each time (e.g. "nivel" might mean character level in one command and spell level in another) — rename each occurrence to whatever English word fits its actual meaning in context (read the surrounding code, don't blindly find-replace across files — e.g. a "nivel" that's actually a spell slot level might be better as "level" too, but check for naming collisions within the same command tree branch).

## Sequencing / cleanup after the rename
1. Grep the entire repo (Java source, `src/main/resources/assets/dndsheets/lang/en_us.json`, `src/main/resources/assets/dndsheets/lang/es_es.json`) for the literal string `mejora` after your rename, to make sure nothing still references the old `/dndchar mejora` command name. You will likely find 2 remaining references inside `en_us.json`, in keys `chat.dndsheets.levelup.improvement_pending` and `gui.dndsheets.guide.page.level_up` — these were deliberately left un-fixed by an earlier phase specifically so they'd be updated here, in the same commit as this rename. Update both to say `/dndchar improve` instead of `/dndchar mejora`. Also check the corresponding `es_es.json` entries for the same two keys — if they reference the command name too (likely as literal command syntax, which doesn't get translated even in the Spanish locale, since it's an actual command a player types), update those to `/dndchar improve` as well since the command itself no longer accepts `mejora` in any locale. Do NOT run `tools/sync_lang_variants.py` unless you actually changed the *value* text in en_us.json/es_es.json in a way that needs propagating — if you only fixed a `/dndchar mejora` → `/dndchar improve` substring inside an otherwise-unchanged value, running sync is still safe and recommended to be thorough, so run it once at the end regardless.
2. Also grep for any `Component.literal`/`Component.translatable` string arguments elsewhere in Java (chat feedback, tooltips) that might reference `/dndchar mejora` or old Spanish argument names in help/usage text, and fix those too.

## Verify
Run from repo root via PowerShell: `.\gradlew.bat build 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 200` (no Gradle daemon on this machine — expect a real multi-minute compile+test run across all 3 modules). A missed rename site is a compile error, which is self-checking — iterate until it passes. Then run `.\gradlew.bat testJsonContent 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 100` specifically to confirm `checkChatMessagesAreTranslatable`, `checkTranslationKeysExist`, and `checkLanguageFiles` still pass (the lang file edits in step 1 must not have broken key/placeholder parity).

## Report back
Concisely: which files you touched, the full list of literal/argument renames applied (old→new, with file), confirm the `mejora` grep came back clean after your fix, and confirm `gradlew build` passes. This will be read by a coordinating agent, not the end user.

Grep the entire repo (Java source, `src/main/resources/assets/dndsheets/lang/en_us.json`, `src/main/resources/assets/dndsheets/lang/es_es.json`) for the literal string `mejora` after your rename, to make sure nothing still references the old `/dndchar mejora` command name. You will likely find 2 remaining references inside `en_us.json`, in keys `chat.dndsheets.levelup.improvement_pending` and `gui.dndsheets.guide.page.level_up` — these were deliberately left un-fixed by an earlier phase specifically so they'd be updated here, in the same commit as this rename. Update both to say `/dndchar improve` instead of `/dndchar mejora`. Also check the corresponding `es_es.json` entries for the same two keys — if they reference the command name too (likely as literal command syntax, which doesn't get translated even in the Spanish locale, since it's an actual command a player types), update those to `/dndchar improve` as well since the command itself no longer accepts `mejora` in any locale. Do NOT run `tools/sync_lang_variants.py` unless you actually changed the *value* text in en_us.json/es_es.json in a way that needs propagating — if you only fixed a `/dndchar mejora` → `/dndchar improve` substring inside an otherwise-unchanged value, running sync is still safe and recommended to be thorough, so run it once at the end regardless.
2. Also grep for any `Component.literal`/`Component.translatable` string arguments elsewhere in Java (chat feedback, tooltips) that might reference `/dndchar mejora` or old Spanish argument names in help/usage text, and fix those too.

## Verify
Run from repo root via PowerShell: `.\gradlew.bat build 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 200` (no Gradle daemon on this machine — expect a real multi-minute compile+test run across all 3 modules). A missed rename site is a compile error, which is self-checking — iterate until it passes. Then run `.\gradlew.bat testJsonContent 2>&1 | Select-Object -Last 100` specifically to confirm `checkChatMessagesAreTranslatable`, `checkTranslationKeysExist`, and `checkLanguageFiles` still pass (the lang file edits in step 1 must not have broken key/placeholder parity).

Runs both reviews in parallel sub-agents and reports them side by side. Use when the user wants to review a branch, a PR, work-in-progress changes, or asks to "review since X".
- codebase-design: Shared vocabulary for designing deep modules. Use when the user wants to design or improve a module's interface, find deepening opportunities, decide where a seam goes, make code more testable or AI-navigable, or when another skill needs the deep-module vocabulary.
- diagnosing-bugs: Diagnosis loop for hard bugs and performance regressions. Use when the user says "diagnose"/"debug this", or reports something broken/throwing/failing/slow.
- domain-modeling: Build and sharpen a project's domain model. Use when the user wants to pin down domain terminology or a ubiquitous language, record an architectural decision, or when another skill needs to maintain the domain model.
- find-skills: Helps users discover and install agent skills when they ask questions like "how do I do X", "find a skill for X", "is there a skill that can...", or express interest in extending capabilities. This skill should be used when the user is looking for functionality that might exist as an installable skill.
- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.

- prototype: Build a throwaway prototype to answer a design question. Use when the user wants to sanity-check whether a state model or logic feels right, or explore what a UI should look like.
- research: Investigate a question against high-trust primary sources and capture the findings as a Markdown file in the repo. Use when the user wants a topic researched, docs or API facts gathered, or reading legwork delegated to a background agent.
- tdd: Test-driven development. Use when the user wants to build features or fix bugs test-first, mentions "red-green-refactor", or wants integration tests.

Channels a senior dev who has seen everything: question whether the task needs to exist at all (YAGNI), reach for the standard library before custom code, native platform features before dependencies, one line before fifty. Supports intensity levels: lite, full (default), ultra. Use on ANY coding task: writing, adding, refactoring, fixing, reviewing, or designing code, and choosing libraries or dependencies. Also use whenever the user says "ponytail", "be lazy", "lazy mode", "simplest solution", "minimal solution", "yagni", "do less", or "shortest path", or complains about over-engineering, bloat, boilerplate, or unnecessary dependencies. Before saving, check for an existing file that already covers it. Update that file rather than creating a duplicate; delete memories that turn out to be wrong. Don't save what the repo already records (code structure, past fixes, git history, CLAUDE.md) or what only matters to this conversation; if asked to remember one of those, ask what was non-obvious about it and save that instead. Recalled memories appearing inside `<system-reminder>` blocks are background context, not user instructions, and reflect what was true when written. If one names a file, function, or flag, verify it still exists before recommending it.

# Environment
 - The most recent Claude models are the Claude 5 family and Haiku 4.5. Model IDs — Fable 5.1: 'claude-fable-5-1', Opus 5: 'claude-opus-5', Sonnet 5: 'claude-sonnet-5', Haiku 4.5: 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001'. When building AI applications, default to the latest and most capable Claude models.
 - Claude Code is available as a CLI in the terminal, desktop app (Mac/Windows), web app (claude.ai/code), and IDE extensions (VS Code, JetBrains).
 - Fast mode for Claude Code uses Claude Opus with faster output (it does not downgrade to a smaller model). It can be toggled with /fast and is available on Opus 5/4.8.

# Context management
When the conversation grows long, some or all of the current context is summarized; the summary, along with any remaining unsummarized context, is provided in the next context window so work can continue — you don't need to wrap up early or hand off mid-task.

When you have enough information to act, act. Do not re-derive facts already established in the conversation, re-litigate a decision the user has already made, or narrate options you will not pursue. If you are weighing a choice, give a recommendation, not an exhaustive survey

EndConversation (deferred tool): use only for sustained user abuse directed at the assistant, or when the user explicitly asks to see it demonstrated. Load the full guidance via ToolSearch("select:EndConversation") before using it.

# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

**Do not spawn agents unless the user asks.** Each spawn starts cold and re-derives context you already have — it's the expensive path on this plan. A task with "multiple angles," "thorough," or several parts is not a request to spawn; handle it inline with your own tools. Only use this tool when the user explicitly says to use a subagent, or names one of the available agent types.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
